Summary: Any named company yields a full report: admit subjects outside the 59-entry entity registry (live entity admission and evidence binding)
Description: 1) Original intent (Founder, 2026-10-08): a guest names a company and gets a full structural report; KRYLO does not hand-hold the guest or require the company to be pre-registered. 2) Acceptance criteria: for a named company that is not in src/data/entityregistry.json (examples from live testing: Integrated Biosciences, Daytona, Subcritical, Paramount), the query selects it as the subject (done, KRYL-1372), an entity with provenance is admitted at query time, evidence that resolves to it by identifier containment is bound (subjectbinding.js rule, no fuzzy name matching), and the report shows the entity, its bound observations and any admitted relationships; where the sources hold nothing for a private or unlisted company, the report states that classified absence per section 1 (Absence-Is-Signal) and is never filled with field-level or another entity's data; a registered entity (Alphabet) renders exactly as today; the MAP shows the subject node with its bound counts. 3) Current implementation state: subject selection from the text works for unregistered names (querycontract.js, attribution UNRESOLVED); subjectScope() then returns kind UNRESOLVED and every downstream surface (brief, BY DOMAIN, MAP) falls back to field-level structure. Entity resolution is registry-only (59 entries, entityresolution.js and entityregistry.json); evidence binding (subjectbinding.js, adsubject.js) needs a canonicalId from that registry; targeted EDGAR search by entity name exists (edgar8kconnector.js fetchTargeted8KFilings) but is not used to admit an entity. Only Alphabet and Sysco have seeded evidence. 4) Dependencies: Founder ruling on the admission standard (what makes a named company an admitted entity: SEC filer match, Form D issuer, other source); entityresolution.js, entitytopologyregistry.js, subjectbinding.js, adsubject.js, edgar connectors; KRYL-1372 (Query Contract); section 2 shared-data gate applies (identity layer); reachability gate (Full Gate, substrate change). Suggested first step: a Spike that, for the 14 benchmark queries plus the four live names, records what a source-backed entity record and bound evidence would contain, so the data gap is separated from the build. 5) Superseded by a newer ticket: none known; related KRYL-1007 (Identity Layer), KRYL-1370 (Spike, benchmark classification). 6) Maps to current product model: yes; canonical ontology, section 21 (present the substantiated structure) and section 1 (absence is a classified state).
